concepts.title: Components of Computerised Accounting System
concepts.definition: A CAS rests on five pillars: a procedure (the logical order of steps that completes a task), data (the raw facts fed in for a business use), people (the users), hardware (the computer, its peripherals and network) and software (system plus application programs). Processing accounting transactions through this hardware-software pair yields the accounting records and reports: day books and journals, ledger, trial balance, position statement and the statement of profit and loss.
concepts.formula: cas_components = procedure plus data plus people plus hardware plus software
concepts.key_idea: Hardware and software alone are not enough -- procedure, data and people complete the system.
question_patterns: name the five components of a computerised accounting system
which reports does a computerised accounting system generate from transaction inputs
define procedure and data as components of CAS
how does application software differ from system software in a CAS
why are people counted among the components of a computerised accounting system

solution_steps.explain: procedure, data, people, hardware and software are the five pillars of CAS
transactions enter as inputs, accounting software processes them, and journals, ledger, trial balance, balance sheet and profit-loss statement come out

concepts.title: Data Items and the Data-to-Information Conversion
concepts.definition: A data item is the smallest named unit of data in an information system. One accounting transaction carries four such elements: the account name, its accounting code, the transaction date and the amount. Processing turns data into information -- for instance, days worked and rate per day are raw data that multiply into the amount to pay, and the same information can itself serve as data at a higher level for a decision maker.
concepts.key_idea: Raw data elements gain meaning only after processing -- days worked times rate per day becomes the payable amount.
concepts.textbook_ref: leca101.txt, Data and Information with Figure 1.3 (approx lines 85-98)
question_patterns: an employee works 24 days at a rate of Rs 450 per day; compute the amount to pay
convert the data items days worked and rate per day into the payable amount
a worker attends 26 days at Rs 525 per day; what amount should the payroll record
list the four data elements contained in one accounting transaction
how does processed data become information for a decision maker

solution_steps.explain: processing the two data items together converts them into the information the business needs -- the amount to pay

concepts.title: The Accounting Cycle Phases
concepts.definition: The accounting cycle is the sequence of identifying, measuring and communicating financial information: transactions are analysed, journalised, posted to ledger accounts, and a trial balance is drawn; accounts are then reviewed, adjustments are posted to produce an adjusted trial balance, and finally the balance sheet and profit-loss account emerge from the adjusted ledger.
concepts.formula: cycle_order = analyse plus journalise plus post plus trial_balance plus adjust plus final_statements
concepts.key_idea: From analysing a transaction to the final statements, each phase feeds the next in a fixed order.
question_patterns: what are the phases in an accounting cycle
state the steps between recording a journal entry and preparing the balance sheet
why is an adjusted trial balance prepared before the final statements
where are journal entries posted in the accounting cycle
which phase of the accounting cycle precedes the trial balance

solution_steps.explain: analyse transactions, record in journal, post to ledger, prepare trial balance
review accounts, post adjustments, prepare adjusted trial balance, then the balance sheet and profit-loss account

concepts.title: Salient Features of CAS Software
concepts.definition: Good CAS software shows five features: it is simple and integrated, automating sales, finance, purchase, inventory and manufacturing on one platform; transparent and controlled, widening access to day-to-day operational information; accurate and fast, using user-definable entry templates; scalable, handling growing data volumes as the business grows; and reliable, keeping critical financial output accurate, controlled and secured.
concepts.formula: cas_features = integration plus transparency plus accuracy_speed plus scalability plus reliability
concepts.key_idea: Integrated, transparent, fast, scalable and reliable -- five tests any accounting software must pass.
question_patterns: what are the salient features of computerised accounting software
how does scalability of CAS help a growing business
why is integration of business operations valued in CAS
how do user-definable templates improve accuracy and speed of data entry
what does reliability of a CAS ensure for financial information

solution_steps.explain: simple and integrated, transparency and control, accuracy and speed, scalability, reliability
integration unifies operations, transparency widens access, templates speed entry, scalability tracks business size, reliability secures output

concepts.title: Accounting Equation and Grouping of Accounts
concepts.definition: Double-entry accounting rests on the equality of assets and equities, written as A = E where E = L + C, so Assets = Liabilities + Capital. Because owner claims shift with profit or loss, the expanded form reads Assets = Liabilities + Capital + (Revenues - Expenses). Each side then breaks into groups: equity and liabilities (shareholder funds, non-current and current liabilities), assets (non-current and current), revenues (sales and other income) and expenses (material, salary, depreciation, interest and allied heads).
concepts.key_idea: Assets always equal liabilities plus capital, with capital swelled or shrunk by revenues less expenses.
concepts.textbook_ref: leca101.txt, Accounting Equation and group lists (approx lines 175-257)
question_patterns: a firm shows liabilities of Rs 500000, opening capital Rs 300000, revenues Rs 150000 and expenses Rs 90000; find its total assets
state the accounting equation and its expanded form including revenues and expenses
compute the closing capital when opening capital is Rs 200000, revenues are Rs 80000 and expenses are Rs 65000
find the asset total of a firm whose liabilities are Rs 750000 and capital after results is Rs 450000
under which groups are trade payables and trade receivables classified in the expanded equation

solution_steps.explain: owner claims change with success or failure, so revenues raise and expenses lower the capital
the double-entry equality sets total assets equal to liabilities plus the result-carrying capital

concepts.title: Methods of Codification: Sequential, Block and Mnemonic
concepts.definition: A code is a system of letters or figures with an agreed meaning, used for brevity and machine processing. Sequential codes run in consecutive order and suit source documents such as cheques and invoices, making missing numbers easy to spot. Block codes partition a number range into sub-ranges, each reserved for one group of items. Mnemonic codes use alphabetic abbreviations as symbols -- SJ for sales journal, DLH for Delhi -- so the code itself recalls the item.
concepts.formula: code_types = sequential plus block plus mnemonic
concepts.key_idea: Pick the code style by purpose: order for documents, ranges for groups, abbreviations for recall.
question_patterns: distinguish sequential, block and mnemonic codes with one example each
which codification method suits source documents like cheques and invoices and why
how does a block code assign sub-ranges to dealer types
what makes DLH for Delhi a mnemonic code
how do sequential codes help in tracing a missing document

solution_steps.explain: sequential assigns consecutive numbers, block reserves number ranges for groups, mnemonic uses letter abbreviations
invoices and cheques take sequential codes, dealer or item classes take blocks, stations and journals take mnemonic symbols

concepts.title: Block Code Range Capacity
concepts.definition: A block code reserves a consecutive number band for one group -- for a trading firm, 100-199 might hold small pumps, 200-299 medium pumps, 300-399 pipes and 400-499 motors. The holding capacity of any band is found by counting every number from its start to its end, both inclusive.
concepts.key_idea: Codes in a block run from start to end inclusive, so capacity is end minus start plus one.
concepts.textbook_ref: leca101.txt, block code dealer example (approx lines 325-344)
question_patterns: a dealer block runs from 400 to 499; how many codes does the block hold
calculate the capacity of the code range 200 to 299 reserved for medium pumps
how many account codes fit in a block spanning 300 to 399
find the number of codes available when a block starts at 100 and ends at 199
compute the size of the sub-range allotted to pipes if it spans 300 to 349

solution_steps.explain: subtracting the start from the end drops both ends, so one is added back to include them

concepts.title: Sequential Code Gap Detection
concepts.definition: Because sequential codes assign consecutive numbers to source documents, the assigned band length compared with the documents actually issued exposes gaps. Counting the numbers the band should hold and subtracting the documents on hand gives the count of missing codes -- the first step in tracing a lost cheque or invoice.
concepts.key_idea: Band length minus documents issued reveals how many sequential codes are missing.
concepts.textbook_ref: leca101.txt, sequential codes and document search (approx lines 309-324)
question_patterns: cheque numbers run from 101 to 150 but only 45 cheques were issued; how many are missing
invoices are numbered 1001 to 1050 and 47 were raised; find the count of missing invoices
calculate the missing sequential codes when the band 200 to 249 shows 48 documents issued
a receipt book spans 01 to 50 and 6 leaves are unaccounted; how many leaves remain to trace
how many documents are unissued in the numbered run 500 to 549 when 50 were issued

solution_steps.explain: the run from first to last number, both inclusive, should hold last minus first plus one documents
the shortfall between what the band should hold and what was issued is the missing count

concepts.title: Designing a Hierarchical Coding Structure
concepts.definition: Coding begins with a structure: fix the hierarchy (trust, school, entry-year, stream, class, section, student), then allot digits to each field according to its maximum size -- two digits for up to 99 schools, two for entry-year, one for stream, two for class, one for section, two for roll number, giving a ten-digit student code. The top-level account grouping similarly uses first and second digits (1 for equity and liabilities, 2 for assets, with gaps left for flexibility), so listing codes in ascending order reproduces the desired hierarchy automatically.
concepts.formula: code_length = school_digits + year_digits + stream_digits + class_digits + section_digits + roll_digits
concepts.key_idea: Allot digits field by field according to the maximum each field must hold, then join them in hierarchy order.
question_patterns: the school plan allots 2 digits each to school and entry year, 1 to stream, 2 each to class and roll number and 1 to section; find the total code length
an inventory of 7000 items in 37 categories with up to 40 sub-categories and at most 1000 items each needs 2, 2 and 3 digits; compute the code length
develop a coding structure for students of seven schools and state how many digits the code needs
why does the second digit of the account code jump from 1 to 3 after shareholder funds
how does ascending order of hierarchical account codes produce the balance sheet grouping

solution_steps.explain: each field of the hierarchy contributes its allotted digits to the full code
solution_steps.compute: code_length = school_digits + year_digits + stream_digits + class_digits + section_digits + roll_digits

concepts.title: Security Features: Password, Data Audit and Data Vault
concepts.definition: Accounting software guards data three ways. Password security is the key that grants access, with user rights set by organisation policy so a person may reach one data set and be denied another. Data audit records who changed what in the original data, fixing responsibility and preserving integrity like an audit trail. Data vault adds encryption, which scrambles information so thoroughly that intercepted data cannot be decoded or interpreted.
concepts.formula: data_defence = password plus audit_trail plus encryption
concepts.key_idea: Passwords gate entry, audits name the changer, and encryption keeps stolen data unreadable.
concepts.textbook_ref: leca101.txt, security features and encryption note (approx lines 437-477)
question_patterns: what is encryption and how is it helpful in a computerised accounting system
how do user rights work under password security in CAS
what does the data audit feature record and why does it matter
distinguish a data vault from password protection
why must confidentiality of accounting data be maintained and by which features

solution_steps.explain: password admits users per policy, data audit logs changes and their makers, encryption scrambles stored or moving data
together they deliver the confidentiality and data integrity that CAS promises

concepts.title: Advantages and Limitations of CAS
concepts.definition: CAS advantages: timely reports in the desired format, efficient record keeping, effective system control, economical data processing and confidentiality of data. Its limitations: technology obsolesces fast and forces repeat investment, power interruptions can lose or corrupt data, hacking threatens stored records, and reports that were never programmed or specified cannot be generated at all.
concepts.formula: cas_tradeoff = speed plus control plus confidentiality against obsolescence plus data_loss plus hacking
concepts.key_idea: Computers buy speed, control and confidentiality but demand fresh investment and expose data to new risks.
question_patterns: state the advantages of a computerised accounting system
what are the limitations of CAS software
why does faster obsolescence of technology raise CAS costs
how can power interruptions harm computerised accounting records
why can un-programmed reports not be generated by CAS

solution_steps.explain: timely formatted reports, efficient records, effective control, economical processing, confidential data
rapid technology obsolescence, data loss from power cuts, hacking exposure, and no output beyond programmed reports

concepts.title: Sub-systems of the Accounting Information System
concepts.definition: An AIS is implemented through CAS as an integration of twelve sub-systems: cash and bank, sales and accounts receivable, inventory, purchase and accounts payable, payroll accounting, fixed assets accounting, expense accounting, tax accounting, final accounts, costing, budget, and the management information system. Each owns a slice of the work -- from electronic fund transfers and ageing schedules of debtors to wage bills, depreciation reports, VAT compliance and customised decision-support reports.
concepts.formula: ais = cash plus sales plus inventory plus purchase plus payroll plus assets plus expense plus tax plus final_accounts plus costing plus budget plus mis
concepts.key_idea: Twelve specialised sub-systems integrate into one accounting information system for the whole business.
question_patterns: name the sub-systems integrated in an accounting information system
which AIS sub-system handles the ageing schedule of debtors
what details does a typical wage report of the payroll sub-system carry
how does the fixed assets sub-system report depreciation and book value
what does the management information sub-system contribute to decision-making

solution_steps.explain: cash and bank, sales receivables, inventory, purchase payables, payroll, fixed assets, expense, tax, final accounts, costing, budget and MIS

receipts and transfers, collection and ageing reports, valuation, creditor schedules, wage bills, book values, expense groups, tax compliance, final statements, cost changes, budget comparisons and managerial reports
